answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, slowly released stake before its votes count, then slash that stake when a challenge proves coordinated identities reused the same credentials or funding trail. A glacier-like release delay makes it hard to recycle capital quickly, while independent checks treat a nebula of new accounts as one cluster when their signal links converge. The attacker must therefore tie up real value and risk losing it, not merely mint usernames; the mechanism raises the cost but cannot stop well-funded collusion outright.
